Balasubramanian-Kasiviswanathan arXiv:2610.07728v2 abstract claims C_P(mu)<=25. These are publication/theorem-statement checks, not complete proof certification.

The inequality uses Euclidean gradient energy and locally Lipschitz L2 test functions

statement: For every p>=2, the affine isotropic normalization (U,V) of the two-dimensional law with density proportional to exp(-x) 1{x>=|y|^p} satisfies, for f(u,v)=u, joint Dirichlet energy 1 and conditional-mean marginal Dirichlet energy D_p=p^2 Gamma(3/p) Gamma(2-1/p)/[(1+1/p) Gamma(1/p)^2], with D_p/p -> 1/3. Thus there is no universal finite Sobolev energy bound for coordinate conditional averaging even among isotropic log-concave laws in dimension two.
assumptions: Density is with respect to Lebesgue measure on R^2
Conditional expectation is taken in the V coordinate after the stated affine whitening
Dirichlet energy uses the inherited Euclidean gradients
proof_or_counterexample: Independent normalization, density factorization, moment integrals, derivative calculation and Gamma asymptotic in REVIEW_PACKET.md; two-mesh direct quadrature in verify_packet.py.
remaining_gap: A direct conditional-mean variance estimate or an additional score/transport condition is not proved; a second eligible review is needed for global landing.
verdict: KEEP the obstruction; DROP any promotion to KLS refutation or solution

statement: For X=Exp(1)-1, Y=X+sqrt(t) Z with independent standard Gaussian Z and any fixed t>0, the isotropic log-concave prior has ess sup_y Var(X|Y=y)/t=1. Therefore no universal theta<1 can bound all Gaussian-posterior covariance operators by theta t I for all isotropic log-concave priors, even in dimension one.
assumptions: t>0 fixed
Gaussian noise independent of X
The essential supremum uses the law of Y
Conditional laws retain the original Euclidean metric
proof_or_counterexample: Posterior is a N(y-t,t) law truncated below -1; exact variance t[1+alpha lambda(alpha)-lambda(alpha)^2] tends to t on positive-probability right tails. Full analytic proof in ATTEMPT.md; 15 finite numerical cases are illustrative only.
remaining_gap: Own contribution requires w356 audit. This refutes only a pointwise covariance margin; it does not refute an averaged gradient-energy contraction or prove KLS.
verdict: KEEP candidate obstruction pending independent review

statement: For the channel Y=sqrt(t)X+G, a finite prior Poincare constant C implies R_mu(t)>=1/(1+Ct). Conversely, if mu is full-dimensional log-concave and R_mu(t0)>=eta>0 over all centered L2 tests, then C_P(mu)<=1/(eta t0).
assumptions: t,t0>0; G standard Gaussian independent of X
A assumes a finite Poincare inequality on the Sobolev domain
B assumes the generalized strongly log-concave posterior Poincare inequality, including convex support
Retention is the infimum over all nonconstant L2 functions, not a selected test class

source.author: w350
source.external_input: generalized Brascamp-Lieb/Poincare for t0-strongly log-concave posterior

proof_or_counterexample: Independent check: Bessel on Gaussian coordinate functions gives |grad T g|^2<=t Var(g(Y)|X=x); total variance and the assumed prior Poincare inequality give ||T||^2<=Ct/(1+Ct) on centered L2. The adjoint is T*f=E[f(X)|Y] by the joint-law pairing, so q_f>=Var(f)/(1+Ct). For B, posterior curvature is t0, hence q_f<=t0^{-1} E|grad f|^2 by posterior Poincare and the tower property; combine with q_f>=eta Var(f). Smooth bounded tests are dense in L2(Y); ordinary Sobolev approximation handles the energy domain.
remaining_gap: The dimension-uniform retention premise VR is unproved here and equivalent to the target up to constants. The external generalized posterior inequality needs an exact primary locator before final publication.
verdict: KEEP A and B with stated assumptions; DROP any inference that VR or full KLS is proved

statement: For n=2d and X=(U,V) uniform on the isotropic ball of radius sqrt(n+2), the polynomial f=|U|^2-|V|^2 satisfies Var(f)/[E Var(f|U)+E Var(f|V)]=(n+4)/4, while Var(f)/E|grad f|^2=(n+2)/[2(n+4)]. Thus isotropic log-concavity alone does not give a dimension-uniform balanced-block conditional-variance comparison.
assumptions: n=2d with d>=1
U,V are the two equal Euclidean coordinate blocks
conditional variances use the joint uniform ball law
proof_or_counterexample: Independent radial and rotational fourth-moment calculation gives Var|U|^2=Var|V|^2=d and Cov=-d^2/(d+2). Conditional d-ball slices give E[|V|^2|U]=d-d(|U|^2-d)/(d+2), and symmetrically. The two centered conditional projections of f sum to (1+d/(d+2))f; projection orthogonality yields the ratio. E|grad f|^2=4n. Full derivation in REVIEW_PACKET.md.
remaining_gap: This only blocks the unrestricted balanced-block comparison; it does not establish or refute the global Poincare bound. A second eligible review is needed for global landing.
verdict: KEEP exact obstruction; DROP promotion to target solution

statement: A universal isotropic log-concave Poincare bound C is equivalent, by affine normalization, to Var_mu(f)<=C E_mu[grad f^T Cov(mu) grad f] for every full-dimensional log-concave mu with finite positive-definite covariance.
assumptions: full-dimensional log-concave law
locally Lipschitz test with finite variance and covariance-weighted energy
the universal isotropic inequality is assumed, not proved
proof_or_counterexample: Set X=m+Sigma^(1/2)Y and g(y)=f(m+Sigma^(1/2)y); covariance becomes I, variance is unchanged, and |grad_y g|^2=grad_x f^T Sigma grad_x f a.e. Converse takes Sigma=I.
remaining_gap: No universal isotropic bound is supplied by this equivalence.

statement: For a joint law with maximal correlation at most rho<1 between centered U-measurable and V-measurable L2 functions, Var f<=[E Var(f|U)+E Var(f|V)]/(1-rho). With a.e. conditional block Poincare bounds M_U,M_V and slicing, C_P(U,V)<=max(M_U,M_V)/(1-rho).
assumptions: rho bounds all centered measurable functions, not only linear tests
conditional Poincare and Sobolev slicing hold for the Euclidean-gradient corollary
proof_or_counterexample: For centered projections P,Q, a=Pf,b=Qf,S=||a||²+||b||²=<f,a+b>; maximal correlation gives ||a+b||²<=S+2rho||a||||b||<=(1+rho)S. Thus S<=(1+rho)||f||² and the two conditional variances sum to 2||f||²-S>=(1-rho)||f||². Integrate conditional Poincare.
remaining_gap: No dimension-uniform rho gap or conditional bounds are proved for general isotropic log-concave laws; w352's isotropic-ball example blocks a uniform balanced-block comparison without an extra premise.
verdict: KEEP conditional implication; DROP any unconditional KLS inference

statement: For n>=2, an isotropic regular simplex in R^n has an edge direction whose conditional one-dimensional slices, given perpendicular projection, have essential-supremum variance (n+1)(n+2)/6 and Poincare constant 2(n+1)(n+2)/pi².
assumptions: uniform normalized regular simplex
direction parallel to one edge
conditional slice is a uniform interval
proof_or_counterexample: With N=n+1, vertices sqrt(N(N+1))(e_i-1/N) in the sum-zero hyperplane yield covariance I from Dirichlet barycentric covariance. The edge length squared is 2N(N+1); holding all other barycentric coordinates fixed leaves an interval of length L S, S=alpha_0+alpha_1. Uniform interval variance and Neumann gap are L²S²/12 and L²S²/pi². S approaches 1 on positive-measure sets.
remaining_gap: This refutes a pointwise conditional-fiber shortcut for this direction only; it does not determine the global Poincare constant or every basis.

statement: In the L2 normalized simplex, the mean conditional slice Poincare constant is 12/pi², yet the optimal constant in E Var(f|Y)<=B E|partial_e f|² for all admissible f is 2(n+1)(n+2)/pi², the essential supremum of the slice constants.
assumptions: same simplex and edge direction as w351-L2
locally Lipschitz f with finite full gradient energy
only the directional derivative occurs in the proposed inequality
proof_or_counterexample: S~Beta(2,N-2), E S²=6/[N(N+1)], so E c=12/pi². For delta>0 choose smooth nonzero a(Y) supported in an interior projected region S>1-delta, and set f(T,Y)=a(Y)sin(pi T/[L S(Y)]). Conditional variance=a²/2 and directional energy=a² pi²/(2L²S²). Their ratio is >=L²(1-delta)²/pi²; let delta tend to zero. The support avoids S=0, making full transverse energy finite for fixed delta.
remaining_gap: Transverse derivatives can grow with localization; this proves no global KLS obstruction.
verdict: KEEP localized-eigenfunction claim; DROP replacement of essential supremum by mean

statement: For the same isotropic simplex edge coordinate T and perpendicular projection Y, linear cross-covariance vanishes, but their maximal correlation is at least sqrt((N-2)(7N+9)/[3(N-1)(5N+6)]), tending to sqrt(7/15) as N=n+1 tends to infinity.
assumptions: maximal correlation ranges over all centered square-integrable functions of the two blocks
proof_or_counterexample: E[T|Y]=0 gives linear cross-covariance zero. Choose a=T²-1 and b=E[T²|Y]-1. Their squared correlation is Var(b)/Var(a). Beta moment E S⁴=120/[N(N+1)(N+2)(N+3)] and uniform interval E[T⁴|Y]=L⁴S⁴/80 give Var(a)=(N-1)(5N+6)/[(N+2)(N+3)] and Var(b)=(N-2)(7N+9)/[3(N+2)(N+3)].
remaining_gap: This is a lower bound, not the upper maximal-correlation gap required by w351-L1.
